items: Shop with a list. Browsing is how scrolling starts.

carousels.name: 5 reasons 'everyone watches p*rn' still isn't a reason (Ofcom 18%)

slides.title: 5 reasons "everyone watches p*rn" [[still isn't a reason.]]
slides.sub: P*rnhub alone reached 18% of UK adults in one month.

slides.title: Of UK [[adults]]
slides.body: According to Ofcom (2023), P*rnhub reached 18% of UK adults in May 2023 — the most popular p*rn service there. Common? Yes. Harmless? That's a different question.

slides.title: Reasons [[1–2]]
items: Common isn't healthy. Lots of people don't sleep enough either.
"Everyone" isn't you. Your life, your cost.

slides.title: Reasons [[3–5]]
items: Most people never check what it's doing to them.
The crowd won't pay your price — sleep, focus, relationships.
Being different is the whole point of changing.

slides.title: Decide for [[yourself]]
items: Stop using the crowd as your excuse.
Look at your own life honestly.
Ask: is p*rn making it better or worse?
Start today.

carousels.name: 4 reasons accountability partners fail at keeping you off p*rn

slides.title: 4 reasons accountability partners fail [[at keeping you off p*rn.]]
slides.sub: It's usually not the idea. It's the setup.

slides.title: Too [[vague]]
slides.body: "Let me know if you slip" isn't a plan. No schedule, no questions, no follow-up.

slides.title: Too [[polite]]
slides.body: They don't want to pry. You don't want to admit it. So nobody mentions p*rn at all.

slides.title: Reasons [[3–4]]
items: Only after slips. Check-ins should happen on good days too.
Wrong person — someone who jokes it off or judges.

slides.title: Fix [[it]]
items: Set a fixed check-in — same day, same time.
Agree on 3 questions about p*rn you'll always answer.
Report good days, not just bad ones.
Switch partners if it isn't working.

carousels.name: 3 mindset shifts that make quitting p*rn stick

slides.title: 3 mindset shifts that make quitting p*rn [[actually stick.]]
slides.sub: Same goal. A different way of thinking about it.

slides.title: From "can't" to [["don't"]]
slides.body: "I can't watch p*rn" feels like a rule someone gave you. "I don't watch p*rn" is who you are.

slides.title: From punishment to [[practice]]
slides.body: A p*rn slip isn't proof you're bad. They're reps you learn from. Practice gets better. Punishment gets you stuck.

slides.title: From days to [[life]]
slides.body: Counting days is a start. Building a life you don't want to escape from is the finish.

slides.title: Try it [[today]]
items: Say "I don't watch p*rn" out loud once.
Write one lesson from your last slip.
Add one good thing to your day — not just one rule.
Skip counting for a day and notice how it feels.
